An object with no declared policy denies by default under a synthesised policy name

reasons.message: No policy rule allowed read; default deny applies.

cases.title: A rule with no declared principal or channels matches every caller on every channel
An everyone principal matches an unauthenticated caller
A rule naming a single action does not authorise a different action
A wildcard action rule authorises every action it is otherwise eligible for
An authenticated principal does not match an empty user id
An anonymous principal matches only an empty user id
An anonymous principal does not match a signed-in caller
An owner principal matches when the record's ownership field holds the caller
An owner principal also matches the record creator recorded in platform metadata
An owner principal denies a caller who neither owns nor created the record
An owner principal cannot match a request that carries no record
A named role principal matches a caller holding that global role
A role principal matches through declared role inheritance
Role inheritance is transitive across a chain of roles
Role inheritance does not run upwards from an inherited role to the role that inherits it
A role principal denies a caller holding unrelated roles
A group-role principal matches a role carried by any of the caller's groups
A group-role principal denies a caller whose groups carry other roles
A group role is not satisfied by holding the same name as a global role
A user-list principal matches the named user id
A user-list principal denies any user id it does not name
A specific principal with an owner flag matches the record owner without any role
A specific principal's role arm and owner arm are alternatives, not requirements
A specific principal denies a caller matching neither its roles nor its owner flag
An explicit deny wins over a matching allow and reports only the deny reasons
The same allow rule stands when the deny rule's principal does not match
An explicit deny wins over a matching presentation restriction

A readonly field rule wins over a matching row-level allow on update

A field-level allow does not grant row read permission

A field-level allow does not extend to an unnamed field
Read shaping applies field policy to an allowed row read
A state-scoped rule applies in the state it names
A state-scoped rule does not apply in another state
The current state is derived from the record when the request does not state one
A state-scoped rule cannot match when no current state is known
A lifecycle-action rule matches its named action in its named state
A lifecycle-action rule still requires its state scope to hold
A lifecycle-action rule cannot match a transition request naming no action
A lifecycle-action rule with no state scope applies in any state
A channel-scoped rule applies on a channel it declares
A channel-scoped rule does not apply on a channel it omits
A channel named on the request overrides the runtime context channel
An import-only rule authorises the import channel and nothing else
An import-only rule does not authorise the same action on the ui channel
A rule declaring no channels applies on every channel including sync
A rule condition comparing a field to the runtime user id matches the owner
The same condition denies a caller who is not the record owner
Conditions evaluate the record values overlaid with the requested patch

The same comparison condition withholds the allow above its bound
A conditional deny rule wins over an unconditional allow when its condition holds

A composite condition fails when its negated branch is violated
A view context mode selects the default read-model source scope
A context-scoped role authorises a record in the same context instance
A context-scoped role does not authorise a record in another context instance
A selected context suppresses scoped roles held for other instances
A global role authorises any context instance, unlike a scoped role

A scoped record is refused outside the selected business context even with a role for it
A scoped create naming another context instance is refused before any write
With no selected context a scoped search spans every context instance the caller holds a role for
A global role does not bypass context scope on a scoped search
An all-mode read model resolves context roles from the membership object across every membership
An all-mode read model returns nothing to a caller with no membership
A required-mode read model reports only the selected context instance
An explicit deny is classified explicitDeny regardless of the rule's name
A refusal with no rule behind it is classified defaultDeny
A hidden or policy-denied field is omitted from the read, not merely masked
